entry.title: Portfolio Rebalancing
entry.summary: Having recently rebalanced my financial portfolio, I remembered that I've been meaning to write about the ways in which I periodically rebalance my life portfolio, too. I first sketched out the idea of a life portfolio about eight years ago, asserting somewhat arbitrarily (because the areas of life can be sliced and diced in a variety of ways) that for my own purposes I think of my life pursuits as consisting of Health & Vitality, Wealth & Achievement, Love & Caring, Character & Self-Improvement, Wisdom & Sagacity, and Beauty & Creativity. entry.title: Knowing in Your Bones
entry.summary: In a comment on my last post, my friend Kurt Keefner wonders whether Socrates really should be considered a paradigm of the philosopher, since he never wrote a word - and philosophic arguments can't be properly weighed unless they're written down. It just so happens that this very topic was of great concern to Socrates and his student Plato - there's a reason why Plato wrote dialogues as representations of the true path to philosophical insight. In an essay on the philosopher as spiritual guide, Ilsetraut Hadot (wife of Pierre Hadot and a formidable scholar in her own right) just happens to have provided a compelling consideration of this matter, which I've been wanting to comment on for the last few months:...

entry.title: Friendship Facets
entry.summary: In my experience, one of the beautiful things about friendship (broadly speaking - I've always liked the fact that the ancient Greek word φιλία covers a very wide range of personal relationships) is that each friend brings out different facets of my personality (sometimes latent facets or even facets I didn’t know I had!). And these facets can be quite particular: for instance, I am a musical person, but different friends of mine might prefer classical, folk, blues, jazz, rock, or pop, all of which appeal to me if the artists are good (as Duke Ellington said, "there are two kinds of music: the good kind and the other kind"!). Some friends might be more spontaneous, more emotionally sensitive, more organized, more philosophical, more creative, more athletic, or what have you - and they might bring out those qualities in myself when we interact or when they inspire me to try new things. This is why there really is an art of friendship and of great conversation. As I turn more and more away from abstractions and universals, I find myself giving ever closer attention to the private, personal, practical, passionate, and particular. This is where life really happens, and where I find the greatest wisdom and joy....
